plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Widely cultivated for essential oils, culinary use, and ornamental borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June-August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and gardens across temperate North America
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: A majestic aquatic perennial with large, round leaves that rise above the water and spectacular, many-petaled flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a waxy surface that repels water and dirt. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters.
plants.location: Asia, including India, China, Japan, and Vietnam, as well as northern Australia; cultivated in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been known to germinate after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the plant's self-cleaning leaf surface inspired the 'lotus effect' in materials science.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a rough, hairy stem and a large flower head made of hundreds of tiny florets surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky. Grown for seeds, oil, and ornament, and also found as a wild plant in prairies and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (late June-September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated widely in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and the United States
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny flowers arranged in a spiral pattern following the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with large, bowl-shaped flower heads surrounded by showy, colorful bracts and a center of silky bristles. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitats. In the Southern Hemisphere, it blooms during the cooler months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter and spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom around May-September
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape regions of South Africa, in fynbos shrubland
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the protea genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
